changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/7658-toc-code-span-anchor-parity.md`

- names `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` → `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` — edited by this change

  > Seven live headings in this repo's own docs were affected (`content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx`, `packages/cli/README.md`). Pinned against the real render pipeline rather than a second derivation of the slug rules: the new test renders each heading through `MarkdownImpl` and compares `extractToc`'s id to the `id` attribute `rehype-slug` actually emitted.

### `.changeset/7694-chart-series-chart-type-alias-refusal.md`

- names `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` → `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` — edited by this change

  > - **Before:** `series: [{ name: 'revenue', chartType: 'line' }]` validated green through `@object-ui/types/zod` (`safeValidateSchema`, `objectui check` / `objectui validate`, any pipeline that keeps `parse()`'s output) — and the key was gone from the output, so a consumer of the parse result drew that series in the chart's own family, precisely what the author was overriding. On the TypeScript face the key was merely an excess property on a fresh literal; a widened object carrying it assigned structurally. - **After:** the same document REFUSES at `series[i].chartType` (issue code `invalid_type`) with one message on both channels — the parse-time issue and the `.describe()` metadata: `Unrecognized key(s) on this chart series: \`chartType\`. Did you mean \`chartType\` → \`type\`? …` followed by the reason and the remedy. Write `type: 'bar' | 'line' | 'area'`. On the TypeScript face `ChartDataSeries.chartType` is a `?: never` tombstone, so both the fresh literal and the widened assignment are `tsc` errors. - **Both written** (`{ type: 'bar', chartType: 'line' }`) is refused at `chartType` alone — the key is not folded onto `type` and no precedence is minted between the two spellings. - **Which documents to scan.** The narrowing does not stop at `ChartDataSeriesSchema`; it reaches every document through the parents that embed it — `ChartSchema.series` (`zod/data-display.zod.ts`, `z.array(ChartDataSeriesSchema)`) and, one level further out, `ReportSectionSchema.chart` (`zod/reports.zod.ts`, `ChartSchema.optional()`). Authors meet it through `safeValidateSchema()` (`zod/index.zod.ts`, which parses `AnyComponentSchema`) and through the CLI's `objectui validate` command (`packages/cli/src/cli.ts`). In practice: every `chart` node's `series[]`, and every report section whose `chart` carries one.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `2b188faa3` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 2029 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (2658 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/37036873358)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c0dad4b52e5deb52dc93da5e032c9770c937d86c`
Local-runs: none
Rendered: 2026-10-02T17:08Z

PR objectui#11487 (card objectui#11476), judged against triage's ruling `5955124315` ("Ruling: retire"). Read for this record: the card body and all four comments on it; the PR body and its 4-file list; the net diff of the head against `main` (the three-dot diff against current `main` `2b188faa3` is byte-identical to merge-base `2c0ddf226`..head: +55 / −4 over `.changeset/11476-retire-generate-output.md`, `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx`, `packages/cli/src/__tests__/cli-bin.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`); and the check-runs on the head, polled at one-minute intervals until every run had completed. Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; the dev's reverse-verification legs are read as reported, and the head's own check-runs are the gate verdicts.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The published bin's accept set narrows — right.** `objectui generate` (alias `g`) no longer declares `--output DIR`. `packages/cli/src` sets no `allowUnknownOption`, `passThroughOptions`, `allowExcessArguments` or `exitOverride` (grep at the head: none), and the CLI runs commander `^15`, whose default refuses an undeclared option with `error: unknown option '--output'` and a non-zero exit before the action runs. So the retirement is a refusal, not a silent accept, and nothing is written — exactly the ruling's shape: removed at once, no alias window. A bespoke refusal branch would have been a second spelling of what commander already does; none was needed.
2. **`generate --help` narrows — right.** `--output` is gone from the help text; `--from SOURCE` remains and is the lit control in pin 3. The documented-flags table in `cli-bin.test.ts` drops `--output` from the `generate` row, so the docs-to-bin lock stays consistent.
3. **The docs surface narrows — right, and complete.** The `generate` flag table in `content/docs/utilities/cli.mdx` loses its `--output` row, and with it the false default `schemas/` (the only `schemas/` left on the page is the unrelated `objectui validate ./schemas/dashboard.yaml` example). `packages/cli/README.md`'s `generate` section carries no flag table and never named the flag. At the head, `git grep -- '--output'` finds only the new changeset, the new pins and vitest's `--outputFile` in unrelated scripts: no skill, example, workflow or README passes `--output` to `objectui generate`, so no reader is left dangling.
4. **Where `generate` writes is unchanged — right.** `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` is not in the diff; it still writes `objects/NAME.json`, `pages/NAME.json` and `plugins/NAME/index.ts` under the current directory. Pin 2 asserts the exact tree `pages`, `pages/probe.json` for `g page Probe`, which is the ruling's second pin ("still writes where it writes today").
5. **No programmatic export moves — right.** `@object-ui/cli`'s `exports` is `./dist/index.js`, which re-exports `serve` and `init` only; `cli.ts` is the `bin` entry (`tsup` builds `cli` and `index` as separate entries). None of the publish-contract fields in `package.json` changes. The "no exported symbol moves" sentence in the PR body and the changeset holds.
6. **`--from SOURCE` left untouched — right.** The ruling names `--output` only. `--from` is a separate declared-but-unimplemented flag, carried out of scope by the dev and now filed as its own card (see ③).
7. **The pins pin the ruling, through the built bin — right.** Three pins under `generate refuses the retired --output flag (objectui#11476)`: the refusal (exit non-zero, stderr matches `unknown option` and contains `--output`, the work directory stays empty), the control (exit 0, exact tree) and the help (no `--output`, with `--from` as the lit control). They spawn `dist/cli.js` as a child process, which is where the card measured the defect. `readdirSync` with `recursive: true` needs Node 20 or later; the repo's `engines` pins Node at 22.11 or later and CI runs Node 22.x. The dev's reverse verification is read, not re-run: BASE dist 2 failed / 41 passed on the two predicted names; the ablation re-planted the BASE blob (the diff's own index line for `cli.ts`, `3b73365ae..6b9bbbbf7`, names the same two blobs the dev reports) and failed the same two; restored, 43 passed. `cli-bin.test.ts` is not in the `dist` vitest project (that project is the components dist-pin glob), so the pins are judged by the eight `Test (shard N/8)` runs on the head (tally below).
8. **Serial and base — right.** `5429e6c74` (PR #11473, the ruling's named predecessor) is an ancestor of the head. `main` has moved three commits past the merge-base `2c0ddf226` (#11481, #11485, #11486); `git diff --stat` of that movement over `packages/cli`, `cli.mdx` and the changeset is empty, so not merging `main` was right and the queue's rebuild on current `main` carries no risk from this diff.
9. **Repository surface — right.** One commit; its trailer pair is the model-free pair AGENTS.md prescribes; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green (not a governed surface).

Nothing in the diff is judged wrong.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/11476-retire-generate-output.md` declares `'@object-ui/cli': minor`. The diff removes something an author can write at the command line, so in semver terms it is BREAKING; this repo's release model (AGENTS.md's version-number policy, enforced by `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` behind the `Changeset Bump Policy` check) pins the 39-package fixed group's major to the `@objectstack` major and ships objectui's own breaking changes as `minor` with the break spelled out in the body. So `minor` is right: `patch` would understate a narrowing, and `major` is refused by the gate outside the once-per-objectstack-major sync. The changeset says so itself in its parenthetical.
- The body carries what a breaking changeset owes: the BREAKING banner naming the package, the FROM → TO line with the one-line fix (drop the flag; files land in the per-type layout, e.g. `pages/NAME.json`), the why, the command-line delta (non-zero exit, nothing written, `--help` and the docs row) and `Clause-②: yes`. Every sentence matches the diff and the measured bin behaviour.
- Not a `skip-changeset` case: `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` is published executable source of a released package, so a changeset is owed and present (`Changeset Declaration` green). `Changeset Overwrite Report`, `Changeset Claim Re-read` and `Changeset Fixed Group Check` are green too.
- **`Clause-②:` line — right.** PR body line 3 reads `Clause-②: yes`; the seat's claim `5956180470` and the changeset say the same. It is a narrowing: an option the published bin accepted (and ignored) is now refused. objectui has no gate that reads an arm on the line (at the head, `scripts/`, `.github/` and AGENTS.md hold no `Clause-②` reader; `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs` only asks whether a clause-② verdict exists), and 105 pending changesets at the head carry the bare `Clause-②: yes`, so the spelling follows the repo's own precedent.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report `5957159207`: `open_questions: []`. Its deviations and findings, each answered:

1. `pnpm install --config.engine-strict=false` — brief-directed and local to the dev's container; nothing on the head depends on it. Answered.
2. PR assignee not set (the `--assign` write was refused by the permission layer before any request left) — an administrative mirror outside the contract; the seat's ACCEPT `5957202174` already records it as the seat's own write. Escalated to the seat; no bearing on this verdict.
3. First ablation attempt void (the replacement contained the anchor; the tool refused and restored before the leg ran), second attempt counted — answered: the counted leg restored the BASE blob of `cli.ts` byte-for-byte, so it is a real BASE/head contrast, and the void attempt was reported rather than hidden.
4. `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` could not read the objectui tree; dist arrival proved by `grep -c` on both legs — answered: an adequate substitute for a one-line option removal, and CI's shards judge the built bin independently of the dev's local build.
5. The first `type-check` was killed by a container restart and re-run on the same head — answered: `Type Check` on the head is the gate (tally below).
6. Build and type-check in one locked call, each part exit 0 — reporting only; answered.
7. `origin/main` not merged — answered right in ①.8.
8. Model-free trailer pair instead of the harness's model-named trailer — AGENTS.md's commit-message rule; not a deviation. Answered.
9. `Clause-②: yes` line in the changeset — the repo's precedent (105 pending changesets); answered.
- Out-of-scope finding, `objectui generate --from SOURCE` prints "not yet implemented", exits 0 and writes nothing — escalated: the seat filed it as objectui#11488 (open, created 2026-10-02T16:58Z), same declared-not-enforced family, for triage. Right to leave it out of this diff: the ruling retires `--output` only.
- The seat's correction that draft PR objectui#11069 also edits `cli.mdx` — outside this brief's inputs and not re-read here; the two edits are claimed region-disjoint, and either way a textual overlap is mechanical at merge under the "whichever lands second merges `main`" rule. No contract bearing.
- The dev report's "CI in_progress, not awaited per contract" — answered by the completed set below.

### Check-runs on the head

43 check-runs on `c0dad4b52e5deb52dc93da5e032c9770c937d86c`, every one completed (the aggregate `Test` landed last, at 2026-10-02T17:06Z): **40 success · 3 skipped · 0 failure** (0 cancelled, 0 timed out, 0 neutral, 0 action required).
